context: area works · utilities laid deepest-first in a shared corridor, then kerbs and road layers; zone by zone

brief.intro: New to this project type? The infrastructure package of a development or a city district builds everything under and on the roads: sewer, stormwater, potable water, irrigation, fire water, gas, district cooling, power cables, street lighting and telecom, then the kerbs, road layers, footpaths and landscape strips. Each network has its own page in this library; this page is about putting them together. They share one corridor, so the order is fixed by depth and by size — deepest and largest first: sewer, then stormwater, then the pressure pipes, then power, and telecom and lighting last and shallowest. Every network must be tested before the next layer covers it, and every road crossing must be in before the road base. The work is released zone by zone, and each network finishes with its own authority's inspection.

must_get_right: Sequence by depth: sewer → stormwater → water / irrigation / fire / cooling / gas → power → telecom and lighting → kerbs → road layers. Anything out of order means digging through a finished service.
Resolve clashes on a combined services drawing before the first trench, especially at junctions where every network crosses every other.
Test each network before the next one buries it, and put every road-crossing duct and sleeve in before the road base.
Lay the final wearing course last, after all utility testing and building connections — and plan the authority inspections and handovers network by network, zone by zone.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by zone and road, and within each road by network in order of depth, so the schedule itself shows the build-up of the corridor.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Standard site calendar; rainy season marked for earthworks and asphalt. Authority inspections, tie-ins and energisations are dated activities.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: In every road: formation → sewer → stormwater → pressure pipes → power → telecom and lighting ducts → sub-base and kerbs → base → binder → footpaths and poles → wearing course. Each network is tested before the next covers it. Zones are staggered so crews move from one to the next. The critical path runs through the deepest utility of the last zone, then the road layers and the authority handovers.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The combined services design is clash-free and approved; authorities attend inspections within the assumed notice; off-site connections (water source, sewer outfall, power feeder) are available on the planned dates.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: All networks share one corridor and one access; open trenches block the road for everyone. Building contractors on the plots need access during the works.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: clashes found during excavation, a late design change by one authority, rain on open excavations, damage to finished utilities by following trades, and late off-site connections. Contingency is held before each zone release and before the final wearing course.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by zone, road and network; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for each utility crew and the road crews — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
